target_customer: Indian EV owners who pay per charging session, and property owners, fleets and partners who host or buy chargers
problem: India had too few public chargers to make EV ownership practical, and property owners lacked an easy way to host and monetise chargers.
business_model: per session charging fees split with property hosts, charger sales, charging station management software and advertising
product_category: EV charging network and charger hardware

founders.name: Akshit Bansal
education: Electrical engineering (self described on the YC page)
previous_startups: Online photo buying company that reached about 50,000 monthly actives, built with Raghav Arora (TechCrunch, Aug 2020)
founders.background_notes: Worked with Arora as a consultant before the photo company, per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Raghav Arora
previous_startups: Online photo buying company with Akshit Bansal
founders.background_notes: YC page says he trained about 1,500 people in India in data analysis with Python.

competitors.name: Tesla Supercharger network
competitors.what: Built its own proprietary fast charging network to solve the chicken and egg problem between EVs and chargers
competitors.traction_then: Named in the TechCrunch launch coverage as the example of the vertically integrated approach, not as a direct rival in India

competitors.name: Better Place
competitors.what: Israeli EV battery swap and charging startup that raised about 800 million dollars and shut down in 2013
competitors.traction_then: Defunct; cited by TechCrunch as a cautionary precedent for charging infrastructure
competitors.funding_then: About 800 million dollars before its 2013 shutdown

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard app and payments software plus locally designed chargers that the founders said cost about a third of comparable US equipment. Hardware, installation and uptime made it harder than pure software.

defensibility.rationale: Host agreements with landlords and a growing charger footprint create local lock in, but chargers are physical assets that well funded utilities and oil companies could also deploy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents and oil marketing companies expanded their own networks; the company instead signed partnership deals, including with HPCL (reported June 2025) and BMW Group India (reported November 2025), rather than being acquired.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in August 2020 described pollution in Delhi, rising two and three wheeler EV adoption among a growing middle class, and government incentive approvals for EVs and charging stations. The founders reported growing 20 percent week over week with more than 150 stations installed.

branding.domain_note: Company site is statiq.in, a country domain, not a .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat and concise slogans such as Reliable, fast and accessible charging, anywhere you go

branding.community_and_virality: No merch or community evidence found; coverage is trade press about partnerships.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated trade and business press coverage and named partnerships with BMW Group India and HPCL show brand recognition in Indian EV charging, but no source credits the name or identity as a growth driver.

pivots.why: The founders researched pollution in Delhi and moved into EVs, per TechCrunch (Aug 2020). The exact month of the pivot is not stated beyond the October 2019 founding.

outcome_analysis: Statiq started in October 2019, launched in May 2020 and reported 20 percent weekly growth at YC. By 2025 trade press put the network at more than 8,000 chargers and described partnerships with HPCL and BMW Group India, and in February 2026 it raised about 18 million dollars of equity and debt led by Tenacity Ventures. No layoffs or exit were found. Capital intensity remains the main risk.
notes: Tesla and Better Place are named in the 2020 TechCrunch piece as analogies, not as Indian rivals. No Indian competitor with a source dated near the batch was opened (a search showed Tata Power, Ather Grid, Fortum, ChargeZone, Magenta, but with undated or later pages), so none are listed. The February 2026 round is a blended equity and debt round with no stated split. Earlier rounds, including any YC standard deal, were not found. Founding year given as 2019 by TechCrunch (October 2019); other sources say 2020.
